heading: Orientation at RMIT
text: Your orientation is all about helping you get to know RMIT, your program, and everything that life at uni has in store for you! Orientation Week (O Week) happens the week before classes kick off—it’s your chance to dive into uni life, get connected, and feel confident before your first class. Orientation includes three key activities designed to help you: Understand your program. Get familiar with your campus. Make connections through events and activities. Make sure you take part in all three. It’s the best way to start your RMIT journey.

heading: Starting at RMIT in Semester 3?
text: Semester 3 Orientation Day will be held in person on campus. You’ll take part in orientation activities and program induction sessions to help you get ready to start. Vocational education (TAFE) students: Thursday 27 August 2026. Higher education students: Thursday 15 October 2026. Make sure you have access to your RMIT email, where you’ll receive your Orientation and induction information. You can also keep an eye on important Semester 3 dates.

heading: The key parts of orientation
text:
To help you settle into RMIT life, make sure you attend each of the three key elements of orientation.

### 1. Complete How2RMIT
Complete the RMIT online onboarding module designed to help you get set up and prepared for RMIT life.

heading: 2. Attend your program induction
text:
Learn about your program structure and requirements, meet academic staff, peers and more. You’ll receive an invitation via email. Keep an eye on your RMIT inbox for more details.

### 3. Go to your campus O Week events
Explore campus, meet other students, enjoy tours and free food, and connect with support services. Keep an eye on your RMIT inbox for event details and updates.

heading: Navigating campus life
text:
Figuring out where your classes are, how to read room numbers, or where to grab a bite can be tricky. Explore the tabs below to get familiar with your campus.

### Getting to campus
Getting to and from campus is simple once you know your options. Whether you’re travelling by public transport, bike or car, the information below will help you plan your trip and understand any costs.

heading: Public transport
text: City campus: The city campus is in the heart of the CBD and is well connected to public transport. Close train stations: Melbourne Central and State Library. Trams run frequently along Swanston Street. Multiple bus routes operate nearby. Brunswick campus: Tram 19 (Coburg North) stops on Sydney Road. Dawson Street is the closest stop. Jewell Station on the Upfield line is a short walk to campus. Bundoora campus: Tram 86 (Bundoora RMIT) stops right outside campus on Plenty Road. Buses run from nearby train stations including Reservoir and Greensborough.

heading: Cycling to campus
text:
RMIT provides secure bike hubs, racks, and end-of-trip facilities like showers and lockers across campuses.

### Parking on campus
Parking is limited across campuses. Paid street parking and commercial parking garages are available nearby.

### Tour your campus
Take a virtual tour of Melbourne City, Brunswick, Bundoora and Point Cook campuses. Melbourne City campus tour: Take a look around RMIT’s Melbourne City Campus! Join our student host, Lily, as she guides you through key student spots like Student Connect, the Library, campus support services, cheap eats and more. Brunswick campus tour: Explore our Brunswick campus, home to design, fashion, and textile programs. Bundoora campus tour: Discover our Bundoora campus, surrounded by parklands and featuring state-of-the-art facilities for health, science, and engineering.

heading: Places and spaces around campus
text:
Explore the different types of spaces available across RMIT’s Brunswick, Bundoora, and Melbourne City campuses to help you study, recharge, and feel supported.

### Study spaces on campus
Whether you’re studying solo or collaborating with classmates, RMIT offers a wide range of study spaces across all campuses. From quiet corners to bookable group rooms, there’s a space to suit your style.

heading: Sensory-friendly spaces
text:
While being on campus is vibrant and full of energy—we know it can be overwhelming for some students. RMIT Libraries include sensory-friendly rooms designed to reduce sensory discomfort and promote calmness. No booking required.

### Make connections
Orientation is the perfect time to start building your uni community. Whether you’re into sport, creativity, culture, or just want to meet new people, RMIT has a huge range of ways to get involved.

heading: Make friends at RMIT
text: Join student-led programs designed to help you feel at home. Whether you’re shy or social, you’ll find opportunities like: Drop-in sessions and chats, City walks and cultural outings, Trivia nights and themed events, Peer support and volunteering opportunities.

heading: Programs, Colleges and locations
text:
Find out which college you belong to and where your classes will be located.

### Reading room numbers
All rooms at RMIT are numbered in the following way: Building number. Floor number. Room number. That means, if the location is 080.04.020, it’s building 80, level 4, room 20.

heading: Programs and courses
text: At RMIT, a program is the qualification you’re studying (e.g., Bachelor of Business), and a course is a subject within that program (e.g., Marketing Principles). Programs are made up of multiple courses and are offered across our colleges and schools.

heading: Colleges and schools
text:
RMIT offers programs across 4 academic colleges and 16 academic schools. A college is a broad academic division grouping related disciplines, while a school focuses on a specific field within that college.

### Cheap eats around your campus
Making the most of the food available on or near your campus can help you stay energised and enjoy uni life. Whether you’re after a quick bite between classes, a coffee catch-up with friends, or something more substantial after a long day, there are plenty of affordable options to explore. RMIT has a range of food retailers across its City, Brunswick, and Bundoora campuses, offering convenient and budget-friendly choices for students.

heading: RMIT Store student discount
text:
Get ready for the semester with RMIT merchandise and study essentials. Enjoy 10% off at the RMIT Store during orientation.

### We’re here to support you
From study support and accommodation advice to mental health services, RMIT has a range of support services to help you throughout your studies.

### Need help?
If you have questions about orientation or starting your studies, contact Student Connect for assistance.
